shots.prompt: Bright spring morning. Wide shot gliding over a white Greek courtyard wedding: garlands, a vine pergola, guests in bright clothes, swallows darting overhead, birdsong.

lines.text: They say I could make rivers stop to listen. I never tried.

shots.prompt: At the head table Eurydice laughs at something Orpheus said, leaning her head on his shoulder; he looks at her as if nothing else exists.

lines.text: I only ever wanted one person to listen, and she always did.

shots.prompt: Eurydice tugs Orpheus's sleeve and nods at his lyre, teasing. Orpheus shakes his head, shy.

lines.text: Play the one about the swallows. The one you made up on the boat.

shots.prompt: Eurydice grins and gestures at the guests, who have all turned expectantly toward them.

lines.text: Then finish it now. Look, everyone's waiting.

shots.prompt: Orpheus plays his lyre, eyes closed. The whole wedding falls silent; swallows land on the pergola to listen; Eurydice rests her chin on her hand, glowing. A tender, simple lyre melody, no dialogue.
Hymen, god of weddings, frowns at his wedding torch: it will not light, only thick grey smoke curls up. He taps it, puzzled and uneasy.

lines.text: My torch won't catch. It's only smoke. That has never happened before.

shots.prompt: Melitta whispers to another guest behind her hand, eyes on the smoking torch.

lines.text: Hymen's torch is smoking. That's a bad sign, isn't it?

shots.prompt: Melitta now stands at the open gate in the sunlight, flowers in her arms, waving excitedly toward the meadow.

lines.text: Eurydice! Come down to the river, it's full of flowers! Come and see!

shots.prompt: Eurydice jumps up, gathers her gown, kisses Orpheus on the head and points at him playfully as she backs away.

lines.text: Wait for me! Orpheus, I'll be right back. Don't you dare stop playing!

shots.prompt: Eurydice runs laughing through waist-high grass and wildflowers toward the sparkling stream, gown and hair flowing, wreath slipping. Tracking shot, golden light.

lines.text: We were married in the spring. That same afternoon she ran through the long grass by the river, laughing...

shots.prompt: Low close shot in the grass: a dark snake coiled among the flowers lifts its head as her bare feet run past, and strikes at her ankle. Quick, not gory.

lines.text: ...and a snake was waiting in it.

shots.prompt: Eurydice gasps and sinks to her knees in the flowers, clutching her ankle, and calls out toward the courtyard.
Orpheus drops his lyre mid-note and sprints out of the courtyard gate and down through the grass, terrified.
Orpheus kneels in the grass and gathers Eurydice into his arms, holding her face.

lines.text: Eurydice! Eurydice, I'm here, I'm here. Look at me.

shots.prompt: Close-up: Eurydice smiles weakly up at him, calm, and slowly closes her eyes. The wind moves the flowers.

lines.text: It's all right. It doesn't hurt anymore. Play me the swallows. I want to hear how it ends.

shots.prompt: Dusk. Orpheus sits alone on a rock by the stream, the lyre silent in his lap, purple sky, the meadow empty. He plucks one slow note.

lines.text: I sang at her funeral. Every bird in Thrace went quiet. It didn't help.

shots.prompt: Orpheus walks into the sea cave at sunrise carrying a small oil lamp, the sea glowing behind him, his shadow stretching ahead into the dark.

lines.text: So I took the old road down at Taenarum, and I kept walking until the light ran out.

shots.prompt: Deep in the cave, darkness, only his lamp. Far ahead, a faint blue-green glow of the Underworld.

lines.text: Nobody comes back from the Underworld. But as far as I know, nobody has ever asked properly.

shots.prompt: Close-up on Orpheus in the lamplight, jaw set, eyes wet but determined. He tightens his grip on the lyre.
